Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the MCAS procedure set for the four reported conduct domains (claims, underwriting, complaints, lawsuits) across all 51 MCAS jurisdictions; escalates definition disputes to the Head of Compliance

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — the NAIC MCAS Data Call and Definitions published for the data year, line by line, plus each participating department's own data-call bulletin (rep: Alaska Division of Insurance MCAS data-call participation; also Alabama and Arkansas), re-read within 30 days of the NAIC posting the new Data Call

In-scope processes.value: Claim intake through close and reopen, new-business underwriting and rating, cancellation and nonrenewal, complaint handling (department-forwarded and direct), lawsuit opening and disposition, and life/annuity replacement and suitability — every process that produces an MCAS count, ratio, day-count or dollar field

In-scope systems.value: Claims system of record for claim counts and payment date stamps, policy admin for exposure and cancellation counts, the complaint case tool for complaint counts, and the matter management system for lawsuits; each named as the authoritative source in the MCAS data dictionary

Compliance procedure documented.value: MCAS Conduct Procedure Manual — one procedure per MCAS schedule (Claims, Underwriting, Complaints, Lawsuits, plus Life/Annuity replacement and suitability), each carrying the Data Call field number, the field definition verbatim, the source system and field, the owner, and the operating rule it enforces (60-day payment clock, closed-without-payment coding, reopen rules)

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and co-signed by the Chief Claims Officer and the Underwriting Director / Manager; re-approved annually within 30 days of the new Data Call and Definitions being published, and out-of-cycle on any state MCAS bulletin that changes a definition

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Procedure refresh must be approved before the data year opens on 1 January so the year is captured on the new definitions; the downstream MCAS submissions it feeds are due 30 April (private passenger auto, homeowners, life, annuity, long-term care, lender-placed) and 30 June (health, disability income, travel, pet, short-term limited duration) per that year's Data Call

Deadline reminders configured.value: Calendar tasks at NAIC Data Call publication + 5 days (gap analysis), + 20 days (redraft complete), + 30 days (approval), and 15 December (pre-data-year readiness confirmation to the Compliance Committee)

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Every approved version of each schedule procedure, the field-level data dictionary, the Data Call gap analysis and the dated approval record retained 7 years from supersession so a market conduct examiner can read the procedure that was in force in any examined data year

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any MCAS field with no owning procedure, any procedure still citing a superseded Data Call definition, and any operating practice found to contradict its procedure is raised as a compliance exception with root cause, owner and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every procedure rewrite triggered by a definition change or an exam criticism, and every closure of a procedure-gap exception

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All MCAS data elements in the current Data Call and Definitions for every line the company reports, and the procedure that claims to govern each one — roughly the full Claims, Underwriting, Complaints and Lawsuits schedules plus the line-specific interrogatories

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on unowned fields and stale definitions — any reported MCAS field with no governing procedure, or a procedure quoting a prior-year definition, is a fail; more than 2 fails in the sample makes the control ineffective and forces a full re-write cycle before the 30 April submission

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is an annual procedure review keyed to the Data Call; the test runs once a year in Q1 ahead of the 30 April filing, plus an out-of-cycle test whenever a state issues a mid-year MCAS definition bulletin

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have authored or approved any sampled MCAS schedule procedure and must not sit in Market Conduct Compliance

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual MCAS procedure-coverage workpaper (field inventory, procedure-to-field map, sample, re-performance notes, walkthrough memos, exceptions) filed in the compliance evidence repository under Market Conduct / MCAS / <data year>

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Procedure manual export with version history, the field-level data dictionary and the Data Call gap analysis, producible as a market conduct exam pre-exam packet response within 10 business days of a call letter

Regulator response path.value: Market Conduct Compliance is the single point of contact for MCAS definition questions to a department; Regulatory Counsel clears any written answer that concedes a mis-stated prior-year field before it leaves the company

checklist.step: Pull the new NAIC MCAS Data Call and Definitions and diff it against last year
actions: Log in to the NAIC MCAS application through NAIC Account Manager with the company's MCAS filing user id and open Reference Materials for the new data year.

Download the Data Call and Definitions PDF and the blank data-entry template for every line the company writes (private passenger auto, homeowners, life, annuity, long-term care, health, lender-placed, travel, pet as applicable).
Run a document compare against the prior data year's PDF and list every added, deleted or reworded field, every changed interrogatory and every changed participation threshold.
Send the diff list to the Chief Claims Officer, the Underwriting Director / Manager, the Complaints Manager and the Litigation Manager with a request for impact confirmation in 10 business days.
Save the PDF, the template and the diff as MCAS-datacall-diff-<data year>.xlsx in the MCAS working folder.
checklist.done: a dated diff listing every changed MCAS field and interrogatory exists and has been issued to the four schedule owners.

checklist.step: Refresh the jurisdiction and line participation matrix for the 51 jurisdictions
actions: Ask Statutory Reporting for direct written premium by state, by writing company NAIC co-code and by MCAS line for the prior calendar year.
Compare each state/line premium to the participation threshold stated in that state's Data Call entry (commonly USD 50,000 direct written premium in the state for the data year).
Mark each of the 51 jurisdictions Participating, Below threshold, or Not a data-call state for each line, and record the premium figure that drove the call.
Flag states within 10 percent of the threshold as Watch so a mid-year premium swing does not create a missed filing.
Publish the matrix to the MCAS working folder and email it to the Regulatory Reporting Manager who owns the submission.
checklist.done: each of the 51 jurisdictions carries a per-line participation call with the premium figure and threshold that supports it.

checklist.step: Build the field-level data dictionary tying every MCAS field to a source system field
actions: Create one dictionary row per MCAS field: Data Call field number, field label, verbatim definition, source system, source table and column, transformation rule, and the owning procedure.
Walk each row with the system owner (claims for claim fields, Policy Admin Ops Lead for exposure and cancellation fields) and have them confirm the column actually holds what the definition asks for.

Mark any field with no clean source as a Derived field and write the derivation in full (for example median days to final payment computed from first-notice date to final payment date on paid claims closed in the data year).
Register the dictionary in the data catalog with the MCAS <data year> tag so lineage is queryable at exam time.
Hand unresolved source gaps to the Business Systems Analyst as a data-remediation ticket.
checklist.done: every MCAS field in the Data Call has a dictionary row with a named source column or a written derivation, and no row is blank.

checklist.step: Rewrite the Claims schedule procedure against the current definitions
actions: Open the Claims schedule of the Data Call and list each reported bucket: claims open at period start, opened, closed with payment, closed without payment, reopened, closed within 0-30, 31-60, 61-90, 91-180, 181-365 and over 365 days.
In ClaimCenter open Administration and confirm the claim status and closure-reason code sets map one-to-one to those buckets; write the code-to-bucket table into the procedure.

Write the operating rules the adjusters must follow: when a claim is coded closed without payment versus withdrawn, when a reopen is a new claim, and which date stamp is the final payment date used for the day-count buckets.
State the 60-day and 91-day payment-timeliness expectations and the escalation to the Claims Director / Manager when a claim passes 60 days without final payment.
Have the Chief Claims Officer confirm in writing that the coding table matches how the desk actually works.
checklist.done: the Claims procedure carries a code-to-bucket table, the final-payment date rule, and written Chief Claims Officer confirmation.

checklist.step: Rewrite the Underwriting schedule procedure covering issuance, cancellation and nonrenewal
actions: List the Underwriting schedule fields: policies in force at period end, new business written, cancellations inside the first 59 days, cancellations after 59 days, company-initiated nonrenewals, and declinations where the line requires them.

In PolicyCenter open the transaction reason-code configuration and map every cancellation and nonrenewal reason code to insured-initiated or company-initiated, since MCAS reports only company-initiated counts in several fields.
Write the rule for counting a policy term versus a policy (MCAS counts per the definition, not per the billing record) and give a worked example for a six-month auto term.
Specify the adverse-action and nonrenewal notice-day requirements the underwriters must meet so the counted transactions are themselves compliant.
Route the draft to the Underwriting Director / Manager for confirmation that the reason-code mapping matches desk practice.
checklist.done: the Underwriting procedure maps every cancellation and nonrenewal reason code to an MCAS field and is confirmed by the Underwriting Director / Manager.

checklist.step: Rewrite the Complaints procedure and pin it to the NAIC complaint definition
actions: Quote the Data Call complaint definition into the procedure and split it into department-forwarded complaints and complaints received directly from the consumer, since MCAS asks for both.

In the complaint case tool confirm a mandatory Source field with the values Department of Insurance, Direct from consumer, Producer, Third party, and a mandatory Reason field aligned to the NAIC complaint reason codes.

Write the intake rule: every department-forwarded complaint is opened as a case the day it is received, with the department file number and the response due date from the department's letter recorded on the case.
Write the reconciliation rule requiring a quarterly tie-out of the internal complaint register to the NAIC Complaints Database System record for the company.
Name the Consumer Affairs Manager as the reviewer of any case closed without a substantive response.
checklist.done: the Complaints procedure carries the verbatim MCAS complaint definition, mandatory Source and Reason capture, and a quarterly CDS reconciliation rule.

checklist.step: Rewrite the Lawsuits procedure so opened and closed suits are counted on the MCAS basis
actions: Quote the Data Call lawsuit definition (suits opened during the period, closed during the period, and closed with consideration for the consumer) into the procedure.

In the matter management system make Jurisdiction state, Filing date, Matter type and Disposition mandatory fields at matter open, and add an MCAS reportable flag defaulting to Yes for first-party and coverage suits.
Write the exclusion rules explicitly: subrogation suits the company brings, and suits where the company is not a named party, are not counted, with the reason recorded on the matter.
Set a monthly control where the Litigation Manager reviews all matters closed that month and confirms the closed-with-consideration flag before the matter is locked.
Have Regulatory Counsel confirm the exclusion rules read consistently with the Data Call definition.
checklist.done: the Lawsuits procedure defines opened, closed and closed-with-consideration counts, names the exclusions, and is confirmed by Regulatory Counsel.

checklist.step: Write the life and annuity replacement and suitability procedure feeding the MCAS interrogatories
actions: List the life and annuity MCAS fields: policies or contracts issued, replacements (internal and external), surrenders, free-look cancellations, and the suitability review interrogatories.

In the policy admin system confirm the replacement indicator is captured at application and distinguishes internal from external replacement, and that the free-look period per state is stored on the contract.
Write the rule for counting a replacement when the replacing carrier notice arrives after issue, including how the prior-period count is restated.
Document the suitability review workflow (producer submission, suitability questionnaire, reviewer decision, decline or issue) and the retained artifact per review.
Confirm with the New Business Case Manager that the replacement indicator is enforced at issue and cannot be left blank.
checklist.done: the life and annuity procedure defines replacement, surrender and free-look counting and the suitability review artifact, with issue-time enforcement confirmed.

checklist.step: Align each procedure to the NAIC Market Regulation Handbook standards it will be examined against
actions: Take the Market Regulation Handbook chapters for claims, underwriting and rating, complaint handling, and producer licensing, and list the examination standards under each.
Add a cross-reference block at the head of each MCAS procedure naming the handbook standards it satisfies.

Where a standard has no procedure behind it (for example claim file documentation standards, or timeliness of acknowledgement), raise the gap to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager rather than writing around it.
Record the cross-reference table in the MCAS working folder so it can be handed to an examiner as an index.
checklist.done: every MCAS procedure names the handbook standards it satisfies and every uncovered standard is raised as a logged gap.

checklist.step: Embed the control points and named evidence artifacts into each procedure
actions: For each procedure define at least one preventive control (mandatory field at capture) and one detective control (periodic reconciliation or supervisory review).
Name the evidence each control produces, where it is stored and how long it is kept, using the artifact name an examiner would ask for.
Register each control in the GRC platform against the MCAS obligation with a performer role, a frequency and a test owner.
Link the control record to the procedure document version so a control test always points at the text in force.
checklist.done: each MCAS procedure has registered preventive and detective controls with named evidence, frequency and performer in the GRC platform.

checklist.step: Have Regulatory Counsel review the definitions against the state data-call bulletins
actions: Read the Alaska, Alabama and Arkansas MCAS data-call bulletins and any other participating-state bulletin that adds a state-specific instruction on top of the NAIC Data Call.
Compare each state overlay to the drafted procedures and mark where a state demands a different count, a different threshold or an extra interrogatory.
Write the state overlay into an appendix to the affected procedure rather than forking the procedure.
Confirm in writing that the procedure set as drafted answers the obligation in all 51 jurisdictions, and note any jurisdiction where the answer is uncertain.
checklist.done: a counsel memo confirms the procedure set against the state data-call bulletins and every state overlay is captured in an appendix.

checklist.step: Approve the procedure set and lock the version
actions: Convene the approval review with the Chief Claims Officer, the Underwriting Director / Manager, the Complaints Manager and the Litigation Manager and clear every open comment.
Sign the approval page recording the data year, the Data Call version the procedures were written against, and the approval date.
Publish the approved set as a locked version in the document repository with the prior version retained and marked superseded, not deleted.
Confirm the approval date falls within 30 days of the Data Call publication and before 1 January of the data year; log a breach if it does not.
checklist.done: a signed, dated approval exists naming the Data Call version, and the approved set is published as a locked version with prior versions retained.

checklist.step: Publish and train the claims, underwriting, complaints and litigation teams
actions: Build one training module per schedule showing the changed definitions and the coding decisions that changed with them.
Assign the modules in the learning management system to every adjuster, underwriter, complaint handler and litigation coordinator whose transactions feed MCAS, with a 30-day completion due date.
Include a short assessment on the changed coding rules and require a pass before the assignment closes.
Send the non-completion list to the Claims Director / Manager and Underwriting Director / Manager weekly until it is empty.
checklist.done: all in-scope performers have completed and passed the schedule training, with the completion report exported and filed.

checklist.step: Refresh the MCAS RACI and the annual attestation register
actions: Update the RACI so each MCAS schedule has one accountable owner, a named data preparer, a named reviewer and a named attesting officer.
Issue an annual attestation to each schedule owner asking them to confirm the procedure reflects actual practice and that they know their MCAS fields.
Chase and collect every attestation before 31 January of the filing year and record refusals or qualifications verbatim.
File the signed attestations with the approved procedure set.
checklist.done: every MCAS schedule has a named accountable owner and a signed, dated attestation on file before 31 January.

checklist.step: Retain the procedure versions and arm the next annual review trigger
actions: Move the approved procedure set, the data dictionary, the Data Call diff, the counsel memo and the attestations into the compliance evidence repository under Market Conduct / MCAS / <data year>.
Apply the 7-year-from-supersession retention label so the version in force in any examined data year survives.
Confirm the repository index makes the record searchable by data year, MCAS line and schedule name.
Set the next-year trigger task to fire on NAIC Data Call publication and assign it to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager.
checklist.done: the data-year procedure record is filed, labelled for 7-year retention, searchable by line and schedule, and next year's review trigger is armed.

testing.step: Build the population of reported MCAS fields and the procedures claiming to govern them
actions: Download the current Data Call and Definitions and the blank template for every line the company reports and extract the full field list, including interrogatories.
Extract the procedure-to-field map from the MCAS data dictionary and join it to the field list.
Reconcile the field count to the template column count line by line and resolve any difference before sampling.
Sign the population as complete and record the Data Call version and download date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the field population reconciles to the NAIC template column counts and is signed as complete by the extractor.

testing.step: Reconcile the procedure inventory to the schedules the company must report
actions: List every schedule required by the participation matrix (Claims, Underwriting, Complaints, Lawsuits, plus line-specific life and annuity schedules).
Match each schedule to an approved procedure version in the document repository and record the approval date.
List any schedule with no procedure, and any procedure whose approval date pre-dates the current Data Call publication, as automatic exceptions.
Confirm the participation matrix itself is dated within the current filing cycle.
testing.done: every required schedule matches an approved, current-cycle procedure or is listed as an exception.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of MCAS fields for definition re-performance
actions: Take 100 percent of the fields the Data Call diff flagged as changed this year.
Take 25 further fields at random from the remaining population using a seeded, reproducible selection, weighted to include at least 5 fields from each schedule.
Record the seed, population size, selection date and the resulting field list in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn.
Confirm the sample includes at least one derived field and one day-count bucket field.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, covers all changed fields and includes derived and day-count fields.

testing.step: Re-perform the definition trace for each sampled field
actions: Read the sampled field's definition in the NAIC Data Call PDF and write your own plain statement of what must be counted before opening the procedure.
Open the governing procedure and compare its counting rule, its coding table and its exclusions to your statement.
Treat right answer with a stale citation as an exception in the same way as a wrong counting rule.
Capture the Data Call definition page and the procedure paragraph side by side into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled field has an independent re-performance note and a captured definition and procedure extract.

testing.step: Test the source mapping in the system of record for a subset of fields
actions: For 10 sampled claims and underwriting fields, open the named source table and column in the system of record and read the actual code values present.
Confirm every code value in production appears in the procedure's code-to-bucket table, and that no code maps to two buckets.
Query for rows where the mapped column is null in the data year and quantify them as a share of the field.
Flag any code found in production but absent from the procedure as an exception, naming the volume it affects.
testing.done: every production code value on the tested fields maps to exactly one MCAS bucket, or the unmapped codes are logged with volumes.

testing.step: Test the participation matrix against actual premium by state and line
actions: Pull direct written premium by state, writing company NAIC co-code and MCAS line for the data year from the warehouse and tie the total to the statutory annual statement state page.
Recompute the participation call for all 51 jurisdictions against the threshold in each state's Data Call entry.
List every state where the recomputed call differs from the recorded call, and every state within 10 percent of the threshold that was not marked Watch.
Confirm no participating state was omitted from the procedure appendix set.
testing.done: the recomputed participation calls agree with the matrix for all 51 jurisdictions or the differences are listed with the premium figures.

testing.step: Walk the procedure with the people who actually do the work
actions: Hold a walkthrough with one adjuster, one underwriter, one complaint handler and one litigation coordinator, each selected without the manager choosing them.
Ask each to code two live transactions in front of you and state which MCAS bucket the transaction lands in and why.
Compare what they do to what the procedure says and record any practice the procedure does not describe.
Treat any case where the performer cannot name the applicable rule as a training and procedure-clarity exception.
testing.done: each schedule has a walkthrough memo comparing actual practice to procedure text, with divergences recorded.

testing.step: Test approval currency, attestations and training completion
actions: Confirm the approval page of each procedure names the current Data Call version and is dated within 30 days of its publication and before 1 January of the data year.
Confirm a signed schedule-owner attestation exists for each schedule and is dated on or before 31 January.
Export the training completion report for the changed-definition modules and compute the completion rate for each in-scope population.
List any performer coding MCAS transactions in the data year with no completed module.
testing.done: approval dates, attestations and training completion are evidenced for every schedule or the gaps are listed by name.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the MCAS field or schedule, what the procedure says, what the Data Call requires and the reporting impact.
Assign a root cause from the fixed set: definition change missed, source mapping wrong, procedure not refreshed, practice diverged, training gap.
Set an owner and a remediation date that lands before the 30 April or 30 June submission for that line.
Carry every open exception into the pre-submission readiness review as a mandatory retest item.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date before the filing deadline and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold for unowned fields and stale definitions.
Write the conclusion (effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective) with the workpaper references that support it.
Have the independent reviewer, who authored and approved none of the sampled procedures, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any ineffective schedules to the Compliance Committee before the MCAS submission is attested and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and a Compliance Committee reporting date exists in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the annual MCAS submission for every participating state and line; holds the NAIC MCAS company administrator role and signs the readiness memo to the attesting officer

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — the NAIC MCAS Data Call and Definitions for the data year plus each participating department's data-call bulletin naming its deadline and threshold (rep: Alaska Division of Insurance MCAS data-call participation; also Alabama and Arkansas), verified before the extract is built and again before submission

In-scope processes.value: MCAS participation determination, per-schedule data extraction, template population, NAIC validation clearing, interrogatory completion, officer attestation, submission and confirmation capture, and any department-requested resubmission

In-scope systems.value: NAIC MCAS application reached through NAIC Account Manager (Company Registration, Data Entry and Upload, Validation, Interrogatories, Attestation, Submit, Filing History), fed by the warehouse extracts from claims, policy admin, complaints and matter management

Compliance procedure documented.value: MCAS Submission Procedure — participation test, extract run order and cut-off, template population, validation error and warning disposition, interrogatory answer sourcing, variance narrative rules, attestation pack and confirmation capture

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance with the Chief Financial Officer acknowledging the officer attestation requirement; reviewed each filing cycle before the first extract runs

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Data year closes 31 December; submission due 30 April for private passenger auto, homeowners, life, annuity, long-term care and lender-placed, and 30 June for health, disability income, travel, pet and short-term limited duration, per that year's Data Call — each state and line tracked as its own deadline row

Deadline reminders configured.value: Filing calendar milestones at 31 January (extracts frozen), 28 February (templates populated), 31 March (validations clear and interrogatories drafted), 15 April (attestation signed), 25 April (all April-deadline states submitted), with the same ladder shifted 60 days for the 30 June lines

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Submitted data files, validation reports, interrogatory answers, variance narratives, the signed attestation and the per-state submission confirmation and filing history export, retained 7 years from the submission date

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any state or line submitted after its deadline, any submission made with unresolved validation warnings, and any post-submission correction is logged as a filing exception with root cause, notification to the department and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every late or corrected MCAS submission and every decision to file with an explained validation warning outstanding

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every state and line combination required to file for the data year per the participation matrix, together with the submitted data file, validation report and confirmation for each

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on missed and late filings — any required state/line not submitted by its 30 April or 30 June deadline is a fail; schedule totals must tie to the source extract to the record, and any unexplained variance over 10 percent against the prior data year without a narrative is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual per state and line; the test runs once per filing cycle immediately after the 30 June deadline so both deadline groups are covered in one pass, with a pre-submission readiness check in March

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have built, populated, validated or submitted any sampled MCAS file

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual MCAS submission test workpaper (participation recomputation, schedule tie-outs, re-computed ratios, confirmation traces, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository under Market Conduct / MCAS / <data year> / Submission testing

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Per-state submission confirmation and filing history export, the submitted data file, the validation report and the signed attestation, producible to a department on request within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Regulatory Reporting answers NAIC MCAS help-desk and department data-quality queries; anything alleging a mis-stated filing is routed to Market Conduct Compliance and cleared by Regulatory Counsel before a corrected filing is submitted

checklist.step: Recompute participation for every state and line before any extract runs
actions: Pull direct written premium for the closed data year by state, writing company NAIC co-code and MCAS line, and tie the total back to the statutory annual statement state page.
Compare each state and line to the threshold in that state's Data Call entry (commonly USD 50,000 direct written premium in the state) and mark Required or Not required.
For any state that is new to the data call this year or has changed its threshold, record the bulletin reference next to the call.
Create one filing calendar row per Required state and line, carrying the deadline of 30 April or 30 June from that line's Data Call.
Send the Required list to the Regulatory Reporting Manager for confirmation before extracts are built.
checklist.done: every state and line carries a Required or Not required call supported by a premium figure, and each Required row has a dated calendar entry.

checklist.step: Refresh company registration and filing contacts in the NAIC MCAS application
actions: Log in to the NAIC MCAS application through NAIC Account Manager and open Company Registration for each writing company NAIC co-code.
Confirm the registered lines match the Required list and add any line the company must now file; remove none without the Regulatory Reporting Manager's written approval.
Update the MCAS filing contact, the attesting officer and the technical contact with current names, titles, email addresses and phone numbers.
Confirm every preparer has an active NAIC user id with MCAS filing rights and that leavers have been removed.
Export the registration screen to PDF and file it as evidence that registration was current before filing.
checklist.done: each co-code is registered for exactly the Required lines with current contacts and an active, correctly permissioned preparer list.

checklist.step: Download the year's blank templates, validation rules and line instructions
actions: From Reference Materials in the MCAS application download the blank data-entry template, the file layout specification and the validation rule list for each Required line.
Compare each template's column list to the prior year and confirm the extract specifications already carry every added column.
Read the interrogatory list for each line and assign each interrogatory to the function that can answer it (claims, underwriting, complaints, legal).
Store the templates and rule lists in the MCAS working folder under the data year so the exact version filed against is preserved.
checklist.done: current-year templates, layouts, validation rules and interrogatory assignments are downloaded, compared to prior year and filed.

checklist.step: Run and freeze the claims extract for the data year
actions: Run the MCAS claims extract for transactions with data-year dates, partitioned by state of risk, writing company and MCAS line.

Produce the reported buckets from the extract: claims open at 1 January, opened during the year, closed with payment, closed without payment, reopened, and closed within 0-30, 31-60, 61-90, 91-180, 181-365 and over 365 days from first notice.
Tie total claims closed and total paid loss to the claims data mart control totals and to the statutory Schedule P paid loss for a reasonableness check, and document any difference.
Freeze the extract as at the 31 January cut-off, name it MCAS-claims-<data year>-frozen and record the run parameters and row count.
Hand the frozen file and the tie-out sheet to the Regulatory Reporting Manager.
checklist.done: a frozen, parameter-documented claims extract exists whose control totals tie to the claims data mart with differences explained.

checklist.step: Run and freeze the underwriting and policy extract
actions: Run the MCAS policy extract for the data year by state, writing company and line, producing policies in force at 31 December, new business written, cancellations within the first 59 days, cancellations after 59 days and company-initiated nonrenewals.
Apply the reason-code to MCAS-field mapping from the Underwriting procedure and reject any transaction whose reason code is unmapped instead of defaulting it.
Tie policies in force and written premium to the policy data mart and to the statutory state page premium, documenting differences.
Freeze the extract at the 31 January cut-off with run parameters and row counts recorded.
checklist.done: a frozen underwriting extract exists with no unmapped reason codes and in-force and premium totals tied to the policy data mart.

checklist.step: Produce the complaints extract and reconcile it to the NAIC Complaints Database System
actions: Extract all complaint cases opened and closed in the data year, split by Source (Department of Insurance versus direct from consumer), state and line.
Pull the company's complaint record from the NAIC Complaints Database System for the same period and match on department file number.
Investigate every department-forwarded complaint present in CDS but absent from the internal register and open the missing case before the extract is frozen.
Document the reconciled counts and the residual differences with the reason for each on the tie-out sheet.
Freeze the complaints extract and hand it to the Regulatory Reporting Manager with the CDS reconciliation attached.
checklist.done: the complaint counts reconcile to the NAIC CDS record with every difference explained, and no CDS complaint is missing from the internal register.

checklist.step: Produce the lawsuits extract on the MCAS counting basis
actions: Extract matters where the MCAS reportable flag is Yes with a filing date or disposition date inside the data year, by state and line.
Split the counts into suits open at 1 January, opened during the year, closed during the year and closed with consideration for the consumer.
Review every matter excluded by the subrogation or not-a-named-party rules and confirm the exclusion reason is recorded on the matter.
Tie the opened-suit count to the outside-counsel new-matter report for the year and explain any difference.
Freeze the extract and attach the exclusion listing.
checklist.done: a frozen lawsuit extract exists on the MCAS basis, tied to the new-matter report, with every exclusion individually reasoned.

checklist.step: Populate the per-state, per-line templates and run the prior-year variance check
actions: Load the frozen extracts into the NAIC template for each state and line, keeping one workbook per co-code and line as the upload unit.

Recompute the derived ratios inside the workbook: percentage of claims closed without payment, percentage of claims paid beyond 60 days, median days to final payment, complaints per 1,000 policies in force and suits per 1,000 claims closed.
Place this year's figures next to the prior data year's filed figures and flag every field moving more than 10 percent or 5 percentage points.
Send each flagged field to the schedule owner and require a written cause (volume growth, catastrophe, system change, coding change) before the file is uploaded.
Lock the workbook and record who populated it and when.
checklist.done: every state and line workbook is populated, ratios recomputed, and every flagged variance carries a written cause from the schedule owner.

checklist.step: Upload to the NAIC MCAS application and clear every validation error and warning
actions: In the MCAS application open Data Entry and Upload for the co-code, line and state and upload the locked workbook or XML file.
Run validation and export the validation report; work every hard error to zero by correcting the source extract, never by editing the template in isolation.
For each soft warning that remains, write the explanation into the comment field on that field, naming the driver and the supporting figure.
Re-upload after each correction and keep every validation report version so the correction trail is visible.
Confirm the file status shows as validated and ready for attestation for every state and line.
checklist.done: every state and line file is validated with zero hard errors and every remaining warning carries a written field-level explanation.

checklist.step: Answer the line interrogatories with sourced, evidenced answers
actions: Open the Interrogatories section for each line and read each question against its Data Call definition before answering.

Collect the answer from the assigned function in writing (for example claims for the use of a third-party administrator, underwriting for the use of credit-based insurance scores, distribution for producer appointment practices).
Enter the answer and record in the working folder who supplied it, on what date and the document that supports it.
Have Regulatory Counsel review any answer that describes a practice a department could challenge before it is saved.
checklist.done: every interrogatory is answered with a named source, a date and a supporting document, and sensitive answers are counsel-reviewed.

checklist.step: Assemble the attestation pack and obtain the officer attestation
actions: Assemble the attestation pack: the populated workbooks, the validation reports, the variance narratives, the interrogatory answer sources and the readiness memo from the Regulatory Reporting Manager.
Walk the attesting officer through the material variances and any warning filed with an explanation, in a recorded meeting.
Have the officer execute the attestation inside the MCAS application for each co-code and line, confirming the data is complete and accurate to their knowledge.
Date the attestation no later than 15 April for the 30 April lines and 15 June for the 30 June lines so submission is not blocked by a signature.
checklist.done: an executed attestation exists in the MCAS application for every co-code and line, dated at least 15 days before its deadline, with the pack retained.

checklist.step: Submit every required state and line and capture the confirmation
actions: Submit each validated, attested file in the MCAS application and record the submission confirmation identifier, the submission timestamp and the state and line it covers.
Open Filing History and export the full submission list for the co-code, then tie it row by row to the Required list from the participation step.
Chase any Required row not showing as submitted the same business day and escalate to the Regulatory Reporting Manager if it cannot be cleared.
Complete all 30 April lines by 25 April and all 30 June lines by 25 June so there is a working buffer before the deadline.
File the Filing History export and the confirmations in the MCAS working folder.
checklist.done: every Required state and line shows a submission confirmation in Filing History dated before its deadline, tied to the Required list with no gaps.

checklist.step: Handle waivers, exemption requests and department follow-up questions
actions: Where a state is Required by threshold but the company genuinely has no reportable activity, submit the state's waiver or zero-activity request through the MCAS application or the department's stated channel before the deadline, not after.
Log every department question or data-quality challenge received after submission with the date received and the stated response date.
Draft the response with the schedule owner, have Market Conduct Compliance review it, and send it inside the department's stated window.
Where a resubmission is required, control it as a correction with a new confirmation identifier and a note of what changed and why.
checklist.done: every waiver, department query and resubmission is logged, answered inside the stated window and carries its own confirmation.

checklist.step: Reconcile the filed figures back into the metric dashboard and the exam file
actions: Load the filed MCAS ratios by state and line into the market conduct dashboard as the official annual data point.
Compare the filed ratios to the quarterly monitored ratios and explain any difference above 2 percentage points, since a divergence usually means the quarterly feed and the filed extract disagree.
Copy the filed workbooks, validation reports and confirmations into the standing market conduct exam file for the data year.
Notify the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager of any state and line now sitting outside the industry benchmark so it is on the radar before a department calls.
checklist.done: filed ratios are loaded to the dashboard, reconciled to the quarterly figures, and copied into the exam file for the data year.

checklist.step: Retain the full submission package for seven years
actions: Move the frozen extracts, populated workbooks, validation reports, interrogatory sources, attestation pack, confirmations and Filing History export into the compliance evidence repository under Market Conduct / MCAS / <data year> / Submission.
Apply the 7-year-from-submission retention label and set the records to legal-hold-eligible so an exam can freeze them.
Confirm the index makes the package searchable by state, MCAS line, co-code and confirmation identifier.
Record the retention application date and the record count in the filing log.
checklist.done: the submission package is filed, labelled for 7-year retention, hold-eligible and searchable by state, line and confirmation identifier.

testing.step: Build the population of state and line filing obligations for the data year
actions: Independently pull direct written premium for the data year by state, co-code and MCAS line and tie it to the statutory annual statement state page.
Apply each state's Data Call threshold yourself to derive the population of required state and line filings across the 51 jurisdictions.
Compare your derived population to the Required list the filing team used and list every difference.
Sign the population as complete, recording the premium source, the extract date and the thresholds applied.
testing.done: an independently derived filing population exists, reconciled to statutory premium and compared line by line to the Required list.

testing.step: Reconcile every required filing to a submission confirmation dated before its deadline
actions: Export Filing History from the NAIC MCAS application for every co-code and match each row to the derived population on state, line and data year.
Read the submission timestamp on each row and compare it to that line's 30 April or 30 June deadline.
List unmatched population rows as missed filings and late timestamps as late filings, with no judgement applied to either.
Confirm each waived or zero-activity state carries a dated waiver acknowledgement rather than simply an absent filing.
testing.done: every required filing is matched to a confirmation dated before its deadline, or is listed as a missed, late or unwaived exception.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of submitted state and line files
actions: Take 100 percent of filings for the three largest states by premium and 100 percent of any state that raised a data-quality query.
Take 20 further state and line filings at random using a seeded, reproducible selection covering every reported line at least once.
Record the seed, population size, selection date and resulting file list in the workpaper.
Confirm the sample includes at least one 30 June deadline line and one filing that was resubmitted.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, covers every line and includes a June-deadline and a resubmitted filing.

testing.step: Tie each sampled filing back to the frozen source extract
actions: Take the submitted file for the sampled state and line from the MCAS application and the frozen extract it was built from.
Compare every schedule total field by field: claims opened, closed with payment, closed without payment, policies in force, cancellations, nonrenewals, complaints and suits.
Any difference to the record is an exception; investigate whether it came from a manual template edit after the extract was frozen.
Capture the comparison sheet showing filed value, extract value and difference into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled filing ties field by field to its frozen extract, or the differences are quantified and their cause identified.

testing.step: Re-extract a claims sample from the system of record and re-perform the bucketing
actions: Select 30 claims from the sampled states, spread across paid, closed-without-payment and reopened outcomes.
Open each claim in ClaimCenter and read the first-notice date, the final payment date, the closure reason and any reopen date directly from the claim file.
Recompute which MCAS day-count bucket and payment bucket the claim belongs in using the Data Call definition, without reference to the extract.
Compare your bucketing to the extract row for that claim and log every disagreement with the claim number.
testing.done: each of the 30 re-performed claims lands in the same MCAS bucket as the filed extract, or the disagreement is logged by claim number.

testing.step: Recompute the reported ratios and the deadline arithmetic
actions: Recompute for each sampled filing: percentage of claims closed without payment, percentage of claims paid beyond 60 days, median days to final payment, complaints per 1,000 policies in force and suits per 1,000 claims closed.
Compare each recomputed ratio to the filed value and treat any difference beyond rounding as an exception.
Recompute the working buffer for each sampled filing as deadline date minus submission date and list any filing submitted with fewer than 5 days to spare.
Check the median calculation specifically, since a mean filed in a median field is a common and material error.
testing.done: every sampled ratio recomputes to the filed value and each filing's submission buffer is quantified.

testing.step: Test validation disposition and variance narratives
actions: Pull the final validation report for each sampled filing and confirm zero hard errors remained at submission.
For each remaining soft warning read the comment field and judge whether the explanation names a driver and a figure rather than restating the warning.
Pull the prior-year filed values for each sampled field and re-run the 10 percent variance flag yourself.
List any field that should have been flagged and carries no narrative from the schedule owner.
testing.done: every sampled filing shows zero hard errors, and every warning and material variance carries a substantive, sourced explanation.

testing.step: Test the attestation, registration and access controls
actions: Confirm an executed officer attestation exists for each sampled co-code and line and is dated before the submission timestamp.
Confirm the attesting officer named in the MCAS application is the officer the procedure designates and holds the title claimed.
Pull the MCAS user list for the co-code and confirm every id with filing rights belongs to a current employee with a business need, and that the preparer and the attester are different people.
List any leaver retaining MCAS filing rights as a control exception.
testing.done: every sampled filing has a valid, pre-submission attestation by the designated officer, with preparer and attester segregated and no leaver access.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the state, line, co-code, the field or filing affected and the regulatory impact.
Assign a root cause from the fixed set: participation missed, extract defect, manual template edit, validation overridden, attestation late, submission late.
Set an owner and a remediation date, and for missed or misstated filings open a corrected-filing assessment with Regulatory Counsel before contacting the department.
Carry every open exception into the next filing cycle's March readiness check as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and, where a filing was wrong, a counsel-cleared correction plan.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report the test
actions: Compute the missed-filing count, the late-filing count and the ratio exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold.
Write the conclusion (effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective) with the workpaper references behind each finding.
Have the independent reviewer, who built, populated and submitted none of the sampled filings, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and every missed or late filing to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, missed and late filing counts and a committee reporting date exists in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the quarterly conduct-metric pack and the outlier review; accountable for escalating any state and line sitting outside the MCAS industry benchmark before it becomes a market analysis inquiry

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — the MCAS ratios and definitions in the current Data Call and Definitions, plus the NAIC published MCAS industry ratio reports and the market analysis ratios used in the Market Regulation Handbook, refreshed each quarter when the NAIC republishes the industry figures

In-scope processes.value: Claims timeliness and closure outcomes, underwriting cancellation and nonrenewal activity, complaint intake and closure, and lawsuit activity, monitored quarterly at state and line grain for all 51 MCAS jurisdictions between annual filings

In-scope systems.value: Market conduct dashboard built over the warehouse conduct mart, refreshed from claims, policy admin, complaint case and matter management feeds, with the NAIC industry benchmark loaded as a comparison table

Compliance procedure documented.value: Conduct Metric Monitoring Procedure — metric definitions matched to MCAS fields, benchmark sources, quarterly refresh and data-quality gates, outlier thresholds, the review forum, and the corrective-action route for a breached threshold

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance with the Chief Claims Officer and Underwriting Director / Manager as consulted parties; thresholds re-approved annually after the NAIC republishes industry ratios

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Quarterly cycle: data cut at quarter end, dashboard refreshed by working day 10, outlier review held by working day 15, corrective actions raised by working day 20, Compliance Committee report at the next sitting — with Q4 output feeding the 30 April and 30 June MCAS submissions

Deadline reminders configured.value: Recurring quarterly tasks at quarter end plus 10, 15 and 20 working days assigned to the BI Developer, the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager and the Compliance Analyst respectively, with an amber alert if the dashboard refresh fails data-quality gates

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Quarterly metric pack, the underlying dashboard extract, the benchmark table version, the outlier review minutes and the corrective actions raised, retained 7 years so an examiner can see the company knew about an adverse trend and what it did

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any state and line breaching an outlier threshold for two consecutive quarters, and any quarter where the pack was not produced or reviewed on time, is logged with root cause, owner and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off closure of every two-quarter threshold breach and any decision to accept an adverse ratio without corrective action

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All quarterly metric packs produced in the year, the state and line metric rows inside them, and the corrective actions those packs generated

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Every quarter must produce a pack reviewed within 15 working days of quarter end; each metric must recompute to the dashboard value within rounding; any state and line more than 1.5 times the MCAS industry benchmark with no corrective action after two quarters is a fail; more than 1 missed quarterly review makes the control ineffective

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is quarterly; the test runs semi-annually over the two most recent quarterly packs, with the second-half test scheduled before the Q4 pack feeds the annual MCAS submission

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have built the dashboard, computed the metrics or chaired the outlier review for any tested quarter

Evidence location for test results.value: Semi-annual conduct-metric monitoring test workpaper (pack inventory, metric recomputation, benchmark trace, action follow-through, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository under Market Conduct / MCAS / Monitoring

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Quarterly metric packs with trend, benchmark comparison and the corrective actions taken, producible as the company's self-monitoring evidence in a market analysis inquiry or exam within 10 business days

Regulator response path.value: Market Conduct Compliance answers a department's market analysis inquiry about an adverse ratio, leading with the quarterly pack that identified it and the corrective action taken; Regulatory Counsel clears the response before it is sent

checklist.step: Define the quarterly metric set so it mirrors the MCAS reported ratios exactly
actions: Take the ratio list from the Data Call and Definitions and define each metric with the same numerator, denominator and date basis the annual filing will use.

Include as a minimum: percentage of claims closed without payment, percentage of claims paid beyond 60 days, median days from first notice to final payment, complaints per 1,000 policies in force, department-forwarded complaints as a share of all complaints, company-initiated nonrenewal rate, and suits opened per 1,000 claims closed.
Set the grain to state by MCAS line by writing company, since a department analyses the company at that grain and a national average hides the problem.
Have the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager sign the metric definition sheet before any build starts.
checklist.done: a signed metric definition sheet exists whose numerators, denominators and grain match the MCAS Data Call ratios.

checklist.step: Load the NAIC industry benchmark as the comparison table
actions: Download the most recent published NAIC MCAS industry ratio report for each line the company writes and record the report version and publication date.
Extract the industry ratio by state and line where published, and the countrywide ratio where a state figure is not available, noting which was used.
Build the benchmark table with an effective-from date so a metric is always compared to the benchmark that was current when it was measured.
Have Regulatory Counsel confirm the benchmark source is a published NAIC figure and not a vendor estimate presented as one.
checklist.done: a dated benchmark table by state and line is loaded, its source named, and stale-benchmark comparisons are impossible.

checklist.step: Build and schedule the quarterly conduct dashboard
actions: Build the conduct mart model over the claims, policy, complaint and matter feeds at state by line by co-code by quarter grain.
Implement each metric exactly as written on the definition sheet, including the median calculation, and unit-test each measure against a hand-computed sample of 20 rows.
Build the dashboard pages: trend by quarter, current quarter versus benchmark, state heat map, and a drill-through to the underlying transaction list.
Schedule the refresh for working day 8 after quarter end and configure a failure alert to the BI / Analytics Manager.
Restrict edit rights to the BI team and give the compliance audience read and drill-through only.
checklist.done: the dashboard refreshes on schedule, every measure passes its hand-computed unit test, and drill-through to transactions works.

checklist.step: Run the data-quality gate before the pack is published
actions: Run the completeness checks: no null state of risk, no null MCAS line, no null closure reason on closed claims, no null Source on complaints, no unmapped cancellation reason codes.
Run the reconciliation checks: claim counts to the claims data mart, policies in force to the policy data mart, complaint counts to the complaint case tool, suit counts to matter management.
Block publication if any completeness check exceeds 0.5 percent nulls or any reconciliation differs by more than 0.5 percent, and raise a data ticket to the Business Systems Analyst.
Record the gate results, including passes, on the quarter's data-quality sheet.
checklist.done: the quarter's data-quality gate is recorded with every check passed, or publication is blocked with a raised data ticket.

checklist.step: Compute and review the claims conduct metrics
actions: Read the claims page of the dashboard for the quarter and list every state and line where the percentage of claims paid beyond 60 days rose more than 3 percentage points quarter on quarter.

Drill through to the underlying claims for each flagged state and line and classify the driver: adjuster capacity, coverage investigation, third-party administrator delay, catastrophe surge, or coding error.
Pull 10 of the slowest claims in each flagged cell and read the file notes to confirm the classification rather than assuming it.
Write the claims commentary block for the pack with the driver, the volume affected and the named claims leader accountable.
checklist.done: every flagged claims cell has a driver confirmed by file review, the affected volume and a named accountable claims leader.

checklist.step: Compute and review the underwriting conduct metrics
actions: Read the underwriting page and list every state and line where the company-initiated nonrenewal rate or the within-59-day cancellation rate exceeds the benchmark by more than 50 percent.
Drill through to the transactions and separate portfolio actions taken deliberately (a filed and approved withdrawal or tightening) from case-by-case underwriting decisions.
For case-by-case decisions, pull 10 files and confirm the adverse-action notice was issued within the state's required notice days and states a permitted reason.
Write the underwriting commentary naming the portfolio action, its filing reference where one exists, and any notice-timing defect found.
checklist.done: every flagged underwriting cell separates deliberate portfolio action from case decisions, with 10 files checked for notice timing and permitted reason.

checklist.step: Compute and review the complaint metrics against the department view
actions: Read the complaint page and list every state and line whose complaints per 1,000 policies in force exceeds the benchmark, and every state where department-forwarded complaints rose quarter on quarter.
Pull the NAIC Complaints Database System record for the quarter and compare the company's complaint index to the internal figure, since the department will use the CDS view.
Group the quarter's complaints by NAIC reason code and name the top three drivers per flagged state with the volume behind each.
Check closure timeliness against each department's stated response window and list any complaint answered late, by department file number.
checklist.done: flagged complaint cells carry the CDS comparison, the top three reason-code drivers and a list of any late department responses.

checklist.step: Compute and review the lawsuit metrics
actions: Read the lawsuit page and list every state and line where suits opened per 1,000 claims closed exceeds the benchmark or rose more than 20 percent quarter on quarter.
Drill into the matters behind each flagged cell and classify them: coverage dispute, claim delay, bad faith allegation, sales practice, or unrelated.
Flag any cluster of matters raising the same allegation against the same practice or the same producer, as that is what draws a targeted exam.
Write the litigation commentary naming the cluster, the practice involved and whether a claims or underwriting change is needed.
checklist.done: every flagged lawsuit cell is classified by allegation type with any repeat-allegation cluster explicitly named.

checklist.step: Apply the outlier thresholds and produce the quarterly pack
actions: Apply the standing thresholds: amber at 1.25 times the benchmark or a 3 percentage point adverse quarter-on-quarter move, red at 1.5 times the benchmark or two consecutive amber quarters.
Assemble the pack: metric summary by line, state heat map, the four commentary blocks, the amber and red list, and the status of every action open from prior quarters.
Rank the red cells by policy or claim volume so remediation effort goes where the consumer impact is largest, not where the ratio is noisiest.
Publish the pack by working day 10 after quarter end to the review distribution list.
checklist.done: the pack is published by working day 10 with every state and line rated green, amber or red and red cells ranked by volume.

checklist.step: Hold the quarterly outlier review and take decisions on the record
actions: Chair the review by working day 15 after quarter end with the Claims Director / Manager, Underwriting Director / Manager, Complaints Manager, Litigation Manager and Regulatory Counsel present.
Take each red cell in turn and require the accountable leader to state the cause and either propose an action or argue why the ratio is acceptable.
Record the decision per cell as Action, Accept with rationale, or Data defect, and never leave a cell undecided.
Minute the meeting with attendees, the decision per red cell and the owner and date for each action, and circulate within 2 business days.
checklist.done: minutes exist within 2 business days showing a recorded decision, owner and date for every red cell.

checklist.step: Drill the root cause behind each red cell carried forward
actions: For each red cell marked Action, run a structured root-cause session with the operating team and the data owner within 10 business days of the review.
Separate genuine conduct issues from measurement issues by re-testing 20 transactions in the cell against the MCAS definition before assuming the process is at fault.
Write the root cause in one sentence naming the process step, the system behaviour or the capacity constraint responsible.
Propose a fix with an expected effect on the metric and the quarter by which the effect should be visible.
checklist.done: every actioned red cell has a written root cause, a proposed fix and the quarter in which the metric should move.

checklist.step: Raise and track the corrective actions
actions: Raise one action record per red cell in the GRC platform linked to the MCAS obligation, carrying the state, line, metric, root cause, owner and target date.
Set the target date inside two quarters so the effect is visible before the annual MCAS filing reports the same ratio to the departments.
Update each action monthly with the current metric value so progress is measured on the metric, not on task completion.
Escalate any action past its target date to the Head of Compliance in the next quarterly pack by name.
checklist.done: each red cell has a tracked action with owner, target date inside two quarters and a monthly metric-based progress update.

checklist.step: Report the quarter to the Compliance Committee
actions: Present the quarter's red and amber list, the movement since last quarter and the open action position to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting.
Call out explicitly any state and line that will be filed to the departments at an adverse ratio in the coming MCAS submission.
Ask the committee to record its decision on any Accept with rationale cell so the acceptance is a governed decision and not a compliance-only view.
File the pack and the committee minute extract in the board portal and the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: the committee minute records the quarter's red list, the accepted cells and the ratios that will be filed adversely.

checklist.step: Feed the quarterly result into the MCAS pre-filing readiness check
actions: Take the Q4 pack and compare each monitored ratio to the ratio the frozen MCAS extract produces for the same state and line.
Investigate any difference above 2 percentage points before the file is uploaded, since it means the monitoring feed and the filing extract disagree on definition or scope.
Give the Head of Compliance the list of state and line ratios that will be filed in the red band so the attestation conversation is informed.
Attach the reconciliation to the attestation pack.
checklist.done: the Q4 monitored ratios reconcile to the MCAS filing extract within 2 percentage points, with the red-band list handed to the attesting chain.

checklist.step: Archive the quarterly pack and its supporting data
actions: Move the pack, the dashboard extract for the quarter, the benchmark table version used, the data-quality gate sheet and the review minutes into the compliance evidence repository under Market Conduct / MCAS / Monitoring / <year> Q<n>.
Apply the 7-year retention label and confirm the pack is searchable by state, line and quarter.
Confirm the archived extract is a static file, not a live dashboard link, so the figures as reviewed can be reproduced years later.
Log the archive date and record count in the monitoring log.
checklist.done: each quarter's pack and static supporting extract is archived, labelled for 7-year retention and searchable by state, line and quarter.

testing.step: Build the population of quarterly packs and monitored metric rows
actions: List every quarter in the test period and locate the archived pack, dashboard extract, data-quality gate sheet and review minutes for each.
Extract the full state by line by metric row set from each archived pack to form the metric population.
Reconcile the state and line row count in each pack to the participation matrix, since a missing state means it was never monitored.
Sign the population as complete and record which quarters had no pack at all.
testing.done: the population lists every quarter's pack and metric rows, reconciled to the participation matrix, with missing quarters named.

testing.step: Reconcile the pack figures to the warehouse conduct mart
actions: Take the archived static extract for each tested quarter and re-run the underlying counts from the warehouse conduct mart for the same period and grain.
Compare claim counts, policies in force, complaint counts and suit counts row by row to the pack.
Treat any difference above 0.5 percent as an exception and trace whether it came from a late-arriving transaction or a definition change.
Confirm the data-quality gate sheet for the quarter records the same reconciliation and that publication was blocked whenever a gate failed.
testing.done: each tested quarter's pack reconciles to the warehouse within 0.5 percent, and every gate failure is shown to have blocked publication.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of metric rows for recomputation
actions: Take 100 percent of red-rated state and line rows and 100 percent of rows carrying an Accept with rationale decision.
Take 25 further rows at random using a seeded, reproducible selection covering every metric and every line at least once.
Record the seed, population size, selection date and resulting row list in the workpaper.
Confirm the sample includes at least one median-based metric and one benchmark-relative metric.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, covers all red and accepted rows and includes median and benchmark-relative metrics.

testing.step: Recompute each sampled metric from raw transactions
actions: For each sampled row pull the underlying transaction list through the dashboard drill-through and export it.
Recompute the metric in a separate workbook from the raw dates and codes, following the definition sheet rather than the dashboard measure.
Compare your figure to the published figure and treat any difference beyond rounding as an exception, paying particular attention to median versus mean and to whether reopened claims were included.
Capture the recomputation workbook into the workpaper with the transaction export attached.
testing.done: each sampled metric recomputes from raw transactions to the published value, or the difference is quantified and its cause named.

testing.step: Trace the benchmark used to the published NAIC source
actions: For each sampled row read the benchmark value used and the benchmark table version stamped on the pack.
Open the published NAIC MCAS industry ratio report named as the source and locate the same state, line and ratio.
Confirm the value matches and that a countrywide figure was only substituted where no state figure is published, with that substitution disclosed on the row.
Treat a vendor or internally estimated benchmark presented as an NAIC figure as an exception regardless of how close the value is.
testing.done: every sampled benchmark traces to the named published NAIC report, with any countrywide substitution disclosed.

testing.step: Re-perform the outlier rating on the sampled rows
actions: Apply the standing thresholds yourself to each sampled row: amber at 1.25 times benchmark or a 3 percentage point adverse move, red at 1.5 times benchmark or two consecutive ambers.
Compare your rating to the published rating and list every row rated more favourably than the thresholds require.
Check the two-consecutive-amber rule specifically by reading the prior quarter's pack for the same state and line.
Capture the rating comparison table into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled row's rating re-performs to the published rating, or the under-rating is listed with the threshold it breached.

testing.step: Test the timeliness of the quarterly cycle
actions: For each tested quarter compute the working days from quarter end to dashboard refresh, to pack publication, to the review meeting and to action creation.
Compare each to the 8, 10, 15 and 20 working day standards and list every breach with the number of days late.
Read the review minutes and confirm the required attendees were present and that every red cell carries a recorded decision.
Treat a quarter with no minutes as a missed review regardless of whether the pack was produced.
testing.done: each quarter's cycle timings are computed against the working-day standards and every missed or undocumented review is listed.

testing.step: Test whether corrective actions actually moved the metric
actions: Pull every action raised from red cells in the test period with its owner, target date, root cause and monthly metric updates.
For each closed action read the metric value in the two quarters after closure and judge whether it moved toward the benchmark.
List actions closed on task completion while the metric was flat or worsening, since that is closure without remediation.
List every action past its target date and confirm it was escalated by name in the following quarterly pack.
testing.done: each closed action is judged on the post-closure metric movement, and premature closures and unescalated overdue actions are listed.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the quarter, state, line and metric and the monitoring failure it represents.
Assign a root cause from the fixed set: measure defect, stale benchmark, gate bypassed, review not held, cell under-rated, action closed without effect.
Set an owner and a remediation date landing before the next quarterly pack is published.
Carry every open exception into the next quarterly review as a standing agenda item.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date before the next pack and a place on the next review agenda.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report the test
actions: Compute the missed-review count, the metric recomputation exception rate and the count of red cells with no effective action.
Write the conclusion (effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective) with the workpaper references supporting each finding.
Have the independent reviewer, who neither built the dashboard nor chaired any tested review, sign the workpaper.

Report the conclusion to the Compliance Committee and, where a red cell will be filed adversely in MCAS, brief the attesting officer before the submission and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and a committee reporting date exists in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the standing market conduct exam file and is the company's single point of contact on an exam call letter across all 51 jurisdictions; escalates scope and privilege questions to Regulatory Counsel

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — the NAIC Market Regulation Handbook examination standards for claims, underwriting and rating, complaint handling, producer licensing and marketing, plus each state's examination authority statute and its MCAS data-call bulletin (rep: Alaska Division of Insurance MCAS data-call participation), re-verified when the Handbook is revised

In-scope processes.value: Continuous maintenance of the exam-ready evidence set for every process a market conduct exam tests: claims handling, underwriting and rating, cancellation and nonrenewal, complaint handling, producer licensing and appointment, marketing and sales, and policyholder service across the 51 jurisdictions

In-scope systems.value: Standing exam file in the evidence repository indexed by Handbook standard, drawing on claims and policy admin for universe extracts, the complaint case tool, matter management, and NIPR for licensing and appointment evidence

Compliance procedure documented.value: Market Conduct Exam Readiness Procedure — exam file index by Handbook standard, standing universe extract specifications, the call-letter response protocol, examiner data-transfer rules, privilege and confidentiality handling, and the annual mock exam

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and Regulatory Counsel jointly, since it governs what leaves the company under examination authority; reviewed annually and after every completed exam

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Continuous obligation with hard event clocks: exam call letter response and coordinator appointment within 10 business days, first universe extracts to the examiner within the period stated in the call letter (commonly 20 to 30 days), individual information requests answered by the date on the request, and the exam file refreshed monthly regardless of exam activity

Deadline reminders configured.value: Monthly refresh task on the last working day; on receipt of a call letter, automatic tasks at day 3 (coordinator named), day 10 (response sent), day 20 (universe extracts staged) and a per-request due-date tracker for every examiner information request

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Exam file contents, universe extracts as delivered, every examiner information request and the response sent, the exam report and the company response, retained 7 years from exam close or the state's own examination record requirement where longer

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any Handbook standard with no evidence in the file, any universe extract that fails its reconciliation, any examiner request answered after its due date, and any file section not refreshed for a quarter is logged with root cause, owner and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off the completeness of the exam file before any universe extract or document set leaves the company, and clears every privilege withholding decision

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every Market Regulation Handbook standard the company is examinable against, the exam file section that answers each, the standing universe extract specifications, and every examiner information request received in the period
