Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on missing sections and late responses — any Handbook standard with no evidence section is a fail, any universe extract failing to reconcile to the system of record is a fail, and any examiner request answered after its due date is a fail; more than 2 fails means the file is not exam-ready and a remediation sprint is opened

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is continuous; the file is tested twice a year by internal audit and once a year through a full mock exam that draws real universes and re-performs an examiner sample

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not maintain any part of the exam file and must not sit in Market Conduct Compliance; the mock exam is run by internal audit or an external examiner, never by the file owner

Evidence location for test results.value: Semi-annual exam readiness workpaper and the annual mock exam report (standard coverage matrix, universe reconciliations, re-performed sample, response timing analysis, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository under Market Conduct / Exam readiness

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Exam file index mapped to Handbook standards, company profile pack, current procedure versions, prior exam findings with closure evidence, and reconciled universe extracts, all producible within the call letter's stated window without a special project

checklist.step: Maintain the exam file index keyed to the Market Regulation Handbook standards
actions: List every examination standard in the Market Regulation Handbook chapters for company operations, complaint handling, marketing and sales, producer licensing, policyholder service, underwriting and rating, and claims.
Create one indexed section per standard in the exam file and record for each the evidence artifact, its owner, its refresh frequency and the date it was last refreshed.
Mark any standard with no evidence as a gap and raise it rather than leaving the section empty.
Review the index on the last working day of each month and chase every section not refreshed within its stated frequency.
checklist.done: every Handbook standard has an indexed exam file section with a named artifact, owner and a refresh date inside its frequency, or a raised gap.

checklist.step: Keep the company profile pack current
actions: Maintain the profile: legal entity chart, each writing company's NAIC co-code and state licences, lines written by state, officers and their titles, and the market conduct organisation chart with named role holders.
Add the third-party landscape: managing general agents, third-party administrators, independent adjusters and vendor claim networks, with the states each operates in and the contract reference.
Record the systems of record for policy, claims, billing, complaints and litigation with a one-paragraph description an examiner can read cold.
Refresh quarterly and immediately on any officer change, entity change or new state licence.
checklist.done: the profile pack shows current entities, licences, officers, delegated third parties and systems, refreshed within the quarter.

checklist.step: Keep the procedure version library exam-retrievable by date
actions: Ensure every claims, underwriting, complaint, litigation and MCAS procedure has each approved version retained with its effective-from and effective-to dates.
Build a retrieval view that answers the examiner's actual question: which procedure was in force on this date for this state and line.
Confirm superseded versions are marked superseded and are not deletable, and that approval pages travel with the document.
Test the retrieval view quarterly by pulling the procedure in force on three random past dates.
checklist.done: the library returns the procedure in force on any past date for any state and line, verified by a quarterly retrieval test.

checklist.step: Maintain and rehearse the standing universe extract specifications
actions: Maintain a ready-to-run extract specification for each universe an examiner asks for: claims closed with payment, claims closed without payment, claims denied, policies issued, policies cancelled, policies nonrenewed, complaints received, and suits opened, each by state, line and period.

Build the extracts to the field layout examiners expect: policy or claim number, insured name, state, line, key dates, amounts, disposition and the file locator that lets the examiner request the underlying file.
Run every specification quarterly against a dummy date range, record the runtime and row counts, and fix anything that breaks before an examiner is waiting on it.
Reconcile each rehearsal extract to the system-of-record control totals and file the reconciliation with the specification.
checklist.done: every universe specification runs on demand, produces the examiner field layout and reconciles to system control totals in the latest quarterly rehearsal.

checklist.step: Keep the complaint register exam-ready and tied to the department view
actions: Maintain the complaint register with, per case, the department file number where applicable, receipt date, response due date, actual response date, reason code, state, line, disposition and the resolution letter.
Reconcile the register to the NAIC Complaints Database System record quarterly and resolve every difference to a named case.
Confirm every closed department complaint has the closing letter and the substantive response attached to the case, since that is the first thing an examiner opens.
Produce and file a quarterly complaint-handling timeliness summary by state showing responses inside and outside each department's window.
checklist.done: the complaint register reconciles to CDS quarterly, every closed department case carries its response letter, and a timeliness summary by state is on file.

checklist.step: Keep producer licensing and appointment evidence current
actions: Run a monthly reconciliation between the producer master and NIPR Producer Database showing licence status, lines of authority, appointment status and appointment effective date by state.
List every producer who wrote business in a state where the appointment effective date is later than the first policy written, since unappointed writing is a standard exam finding.
Confirm terminations were filed with the state within the required window and that the termination reason is recorded.
File the monthly reconciliation and the exception list in the exam file under the producer licensing standard.
checklist.done: a monthly NIPR reconciliation is on file with every unappointed-writing and late-termination exception listed by producer and state.

checklist.step: Keep the rate and form filing approval index available to the exam file
actions: Maintain an index of approved forms and rates by state, line, form number and edition date with the SERFF tracking number and disposition date for each.
Confirm the editions the policy admin system is actually issuing match the approved editions in the index, state by state.
Record the effective-from date of each approved rate revision so an examiner can test whether the rate charged was the rate filed.
Refresh the index quarterly and after every filing disposition.
checklist.done: the index shows every form and rate in use with its SERFF tracking number and approval date, matched to what policy admin is issuing.

checklist.step: Run continuous claim file completeness self-checks
actions: Run a monthly review of 50 claims per major state and line against the Handbook claims standards: timely acknowledgement, timely investigation, timely and accurate payment, proper denial language with the policy provision cited, and complete file documentation.
Score each file and record the defect type where it fails, using the same defect categories an examiner would apply.
Feed defect trends to the Claims Director / Manager with the named adjusters and offices behind them and require coaching evidence.
File the monthly scorecards in the exam file under the claims standards so the company can show it was testing itself before the examiner arrived.
checklist.done: monthly claim file scorecards by state and line are on file with defect types, trends and evidence of coaching action.

checklist.step: Run continuous underwriting file completeness self-checks
actions: Run a monthly review of 50 new business, cancellation and nonrenewal files per major state and line against the underwriting and rating standards.

Test that the rate charged matches the filed and approved rate for the effective date, that the underwriting reason is permitted in that state, and that adverse action and nonrenewal notices were issued with the required days of notice and the required content.
Where a credit-based insurance score or other consumer report was used, confirm the adverse action notice names the reporting agency as required.
File the scorecards and the exception list in the exam file under the underwriting and rating standards.
checklist.done: monthly underwriting scorecards are on file testing rate-charged versus rate-filed, permitted reasons and notice timing and content.

checklist.step: Maintain the prior exam findings and corrective action status pack
actions: Maintain a register of every market conduct exam in the last 7 years by state, with the report, the criticisms, the corrective action plan and the closure evidence for each.
Show current status per criticism: closed with evidence, closed with monitoring, or open with owner and date, and never show a criticism as closed without an attached artifact.
For every closed criticism, hold the post-implementation test that proved the fix worked, since a repeat finding is treated far more seriously than a first one.
Refresh the pack quarterly and whenever a criticism closes.
checklist.done: every prior criticism in the last 7 years shows a status with attached closure evidence and, where closed, a post-implementation test result.

checklist.step: Keep the call-letter response protocol live and rehearsed
actions: Document the protocol: who opens the call letter, who is named exam coordinator within 3 business days, who may speak to the examiner, and how every request and response is logged.
Set the rule that no operating team sends anything to an examiner directly and that every document set is counsel-reviewed before release.
Define the privilege and confidentiality handling: what is produced, what is produced under a confidentiality undertaking, and what is withheld with a stated basis and a log entry.
Rehearse the protocol annually with the named coordinator and deputies so the day-one response is not improvised.
checklist.done: the protocol names the coordinator and deputies, forbids direct operating responses, defines privilege handling and has been rehearsed in the last 12 months.

checklist.step: Stand up the secure examiner data-transfer and workspace arrangements
actions: Maintain a dedicated examiner workspace per exam with access limited to the examiner team, the coordinator and counsel, and full download and access logging enabled.
Define the transfer standard: encrypted transfer only, no consumer personal data by unsecured email, and each delivery logged with the request number, file name, hash and delivery timestamp.
Apply the redaction rules for data that is not within the exam scope and record every redaction with its basis.
Test the workspace provisioning annually so it can be stood up within 2 business days of a call letter.
checklist.done: an examiner workspace can be provisioned within 2 business days with access logging, encrypted transfer and a documented redaction standard.

checklist.step: Run the annual mock market conduct exam
actions: Pick a state and two lines, issue a simulated call letter to the coordinator and start the clock without prior warning to the operating teams.
Request the standard universes and a sample of 50 claim and 50 underwriting files exactly as an examiner would, using the Handbook standards as the test programme.
Time every response against the call letter windows and score the files against the Handbook standards, recording criticisms in examiner language.
Write the mock exam report with criticisms, the response timing analysis and a readiness rating, and present it to the Compliance Committee.
checklist.done: an unannounced mock exam has been run in the last 12 months with a written report, criticisms in examiner language and a readiness rating.

checklist.step: Track exam scheduling, market analysis signals and continuum activity
actions: Maintain a per-state log of examination history, the last exam date, the exam cycle each department applies, and any market analysis contact or information request received.
Treat a department's level one or level two market analysis inquiry as an early exam signal and open a readiness review for that state and line within 10 business days.
Watch the company's MCAS ratio position in states with a short exam cycle and brief the Head of Compliance where an exam looks likely in the next 12 months.
Record every regulator contact with date, department, subject and the response sent.
checklist.done: a per-state exam history and contact log is current, and every market analysis inquiry has triggered a documented readiness review.

checklist.step: Retain the exam file and prove it is retrievable
actions: Hold the exam file in the compliance evidence repository indexed by Handbook standard, state and refresh date, with a 7-year-from-exam-close retention label.
Apply legal hold to any section touching an open exam or a matter under litigation so nothing ages out mid-exam.
Run a quarterly retrieval test pulling five random sections and confirm each opens, is current and carries its owner and refresh date.
Report the retrieval test result and any failed section to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager.
checklist.done: the exam file is retained under a 7-year label with legal hold available, and the latest quarterly retrieval test passed on all five sections.

testing.step: Build the population of Handbook standards and exam file sections
actions: List every Market Regulation Handbook examination standard applicable to the lines and states the company writes, from the Handbook itself rather than from the company's index.
Extract the exam file index with each section's artifact, owner, refresh frequency and last refresh date.
Join the two lists and mark each standard Covered, Covered but stale, or Not covered.
Sign the population as complete, recording the Handbook edition used and the index extract date.
testing.done: every applicable Handbook standard is marked Covered, stale or Not covered against an independently built standard list.

testing.step: Reconcile the exam file to the states and lines actually written
actions: Take the licence and premium position by state, line and writing company from the profile pack and independently confirm it against the statutory state page.
Confirm the exam file holds state-specific evidence wherever a standard is state-specific, such as notice-day requirements and permitted nonrenewal reasons.
List any state written where the file has no state-specific content as an exception.
Confirm the profile pack's officers, third-party administrators and systems list is current as at the test date.
testing.done: every written state and line is represented in the file with state-specific content, or the gap is listed with its premium volume.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of exam file sections and universes
actions: Take 100 percent of sections covering standards criticised in any exam in the last 7 years, since repeat findings carry the greatest exposure.
Take 20 further sections at random using a seeded, reproducible selection covering every Handbook chapter at least once.
Take all 8 standing universe specifications for reconciliation testing.
Record the seed, population size, selection date and the resulting section list in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, covers every Handbook chapter and includes all previously criticised standards and all universe specifications.

testing.step: Re-perform the universe extracts and reconcile them to the systems of record
actions: Run each standing universe specification for a chosen state, line and 12-month period without help from the specification owner.
Reconcile the row counts and amounts to the claims and policy systems of record control totals and to the filed MCAS figures for the same period.
Confirm the output carries the examiner field layout including the file locator, and that no consumer name or identifier field is missing.
Record the runtime and treat any specification that fails to run, fails to reconcile, or omits the file locator as an exception.
testing.done: every universe specification runs unaided, reconciles to system control totals and MCAS figures, and produces the examiner field layout.

testing.step: Re-perform an examiner-style file review on a claims and underwriting sample
actions: Draw 25 claim files and 25 underwriting files from the re-performed universes for the sampled states.

Score each claim file against the Handbook claims standards for acknowledgement timing, investigation timing, payment timing and accuracy, denial language citing the policy provision, and documentation completeness.
Score each underwriting file for rate charged versus rate filed on the effective date, permitted reason, and notice days and content.

Compare your defect rate to the defect rate the company's own monthly self-checks reported for the same period and explain any gap, since a company scoring itself clean while an independent review finds defects is the finding.
testing.done: 50 files are independently scored in examiner language and the defect rate is compared to the company's self-reported rate with the gap explained.

testing.step: Test producer licensing, appointment and filing evidence
actions: Take 25 policies from the sampled underwriting universe and look up the writing producer in the NIPR Producer Database for the state and line as at the policy effective date.
Confirm an active licence with the right line of authority and an appointment effective on or before the policy effective date.
For the same policies, confirm the form edition issued and the rate charged appear in the approved filing index with a SERFF tracking number and a disposition date before the effective date.
List every unappointed writing and every unapproved form or rate as an exception with the policy number.
testing.done: each of the 25 policies traces to a licensed and appointed producer and an approved form edition and rate, or is listed by policy number.

testing.step: Test call-letter response timing on real and simulated requests
actions: Pull every examiner information request received in the period with its due date and the date the response was sent.
Compute days late per request and the share answered on time, and read the responses to confirm they answer the question asked rather than deflecting it.
For the annual mock exam, compare the coordinator appointment date, the response date and the universe staging date to the 3, 10 and 20 day standards.
Confirm every delivery was made through the examiner workspace with a logged request number, file hash and timestamp.
testing.done: response timing is computed for every real and simulated request against the stated standards and every delivery shows a logged transfer record.

testing.step: Test the currency of prior findings, procedures and privilege handling
actions: Take 10 prior exam criticisms shown as closed and open the attached closure evidence and post-implementation test result for each.
Re-test 5 of them against current transactions to confirm the fix is still holding and has not decayed.
Pull the procedure in force on three random past dates from the version library and confirm the retrieval view returns the right version with its approval page.
Read the privilege withholding log and confirm each withholding names a basis and was cleared by Regulatory Counsel.
testing.done: closed criticisms are evidenced and re-tested, past-dated procedures retrieve correctly and every privilege withholding is reasoned and counsel-cleared.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the Handbook standard, the file section or universe affected and the exam exposure it creates.
Assign a root cause from the fixed set: section never built, section stale, universe defect, self-check too lenient, response late, closure unevidenced.
Set an owner and a remediation date, and treat any exception touching a previously criticised standard as high priority with a date inside 30 days.
Carry every open exception into the next mock exam as a mandatory retest item.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner and a remediation date, with previously criticised standards remediated inside 30 days.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report the readiness rating
actions: Compute the standard coverage rate, the universe reconciliation pass rate, the independent file defect rate and the on-time response rate.
Write the conclusion (exam-ready, exam-ready with exceptions, or not exam-ready) with the workpaper references supporting each measure.
Have the independent reviewer, who maintains no part of the exam file, sign the workpaper and the mock exam report.
Report the readiness rating and every not-covered standard to the Compliance Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper and mock exam report with a stated readiness rating and a committee reporting date exist in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the remediation of every market conduct exam criticism and corrective action plan commitment to the date agreed with the department; escalates slipping milestones to the Head of Compliance and the Chief Executive Officer where an order date is at risk

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — the examination report, the corrective action plan or consent order as executed, the state's examination authority and market conduct statutes, and the NAIC Market Regulation Handbook standard behind each criticism (rep: an Alaska Division of Insurance examination arising from MCAS data-call participation), re-read at each milestone review

In-scope processes.value: Draft report review and rebuttal, corrective action plan negotiation, process and system remediation, consumer restitution calculation and payment, penalty payment, retraining, post-implementation effectiveness testing and the proof-of-compliance filing back to the department

In-scope systems.value: Remediation log holding every criticism, commitment, milestone and closure artifact, drawing on claims and policy admin for the affected population, the payment system for restitution, and the general ledger for penalty and restitution accounting

Compliance procedure documented.value: Exam Findings Remediation Procedure — criticism intake and validation, the draft report response window, corrective action plan negotiation and approval, restitution population and calculation standards, milestone tracking, effectiveness testing and proof-of-compliance filing

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and Regulatory Counsel; reviewed annually and immediately after any exam that produces a consent order or a monetary penalty

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Event-driven per exam: the draft report comment window stated in the report (commonly 30 days from receipt), the corrective action plan submission date set by the department, each milestone date in the plan or consent order, the restitution completion date, the penalty payment due date, and the proof-of-compliance or follow-up report date

Deadline reminders configured.value: On report receipt the remediation log auto-creates milestone tasks with reminders at 30, 14 and 3 days before each department-agreed date, plus a weekly overdue report to the Head of Compliance while any exam remains open

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Draft and final reports, the company response, the corrective action plan or consent order, restitution population and calculation files, payment proofs, penalty payment evidence, retraining records, effectiveness test results and the department's closure acknowledgement, retained 7 years from exam close

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any milestone missed against a department-agreed date, any restitution payment made late or short, any criticism closed without effectiveness evidence, and any repeat of a previously remediated finding is logged with root cause, owner and an escalation to the Head of Compliance

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off closure of every criticism, every restitution completion certificate and every proof-of-compliance filing before it is sent to the department

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every criticism and corrective action commitment from every market conduct exam open in the period, together with the affected consumer population, the restitution payments made and the closure artifacts filed

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on missed department-agreed dates and on short restitution — any milestone closed after its agreed date without a documented department extension is a fail, any consumer in the affected population not paid or paid without the required interest is a fail, and any criticism closed without a post-implementation effectiveness test is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is event-driven per exam; the test runs at every milestone closure and comprehensively 90 days after the final closure filing, plus a repeat-finding check at the start of any subsequent exam in the same state

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have owned any remediation action, calculated any restitution or drafted any response to the department

Evidence location for test results.value: Per-exam remediation closure workpaper (commitment inventory, milestone timing, restitution recomputation, effectiveness test results, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository under Market Conduct / Exams / <state> <exam year>

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Remediation log export mapped to each criticism, restitution completion certificate with payment proofs, retraining completion records and effectiveness test results, producible to the department as the proof-of-compliance package on the ordered date

Regulator response path.value: The exam coordinator in Market Conduct Compliance is the sole channel to the department; Regulatory Counsel drafts or clears every response, extension request and admission, and the Head of Compliance signs the proof-of-compliance filing

checklist.step: Log every draft report criticism as a discrete tracked item on receipt
actions: Date-stamp receipt of the draft examination report and immediately compute the last day of the comment window stated in the report, commonly 30 days from receipt.

Split the report into one log record per criticism, carrying the Handbook standard cited, the statute or regulation cited, the error rate the examiner found, the sample size and the population it was drawn from.
Assign each criticism a business owner from claims, underwriting, complaints, distribution or IT, and a compliance partner.
Circulate the log with the comment-window deadline to every owner and require an initial position within 7 calendar days so there is time to rebut.
checklist.done: every criticism is a separate log record with the cited standard, error rate, owner and the comment-window deadline visible to all owners.

checklist.step: Validate each criticism against the underlying files before agreeing or rebutting
actions: Pull every file the examiner cited for the criticism and read it against the standard the examiner applied, not against the company's own view of good practice.
Recompute the examiner's error rate over the same sample and confirm the sample was drawn from the population the examiner names.
Classify each criticism Agreed, Agreed in part with a corrected error rate, or Disputed on fact, and state the file-level evidence behind the classification.
Where a criticism is agreed, extrapolate the error rate to the full population so the true consumer impact is known before the response is written.
checklist.done: each criticism is classified with file-level evidence, the error rate is recomputed, and agreed criticisms carry a population impact estimate.

checklist.step: Draft and file the company response inside the comment window
actions: Draft the response criticism by criticism: accept, accept with a corrected figure, or dispute with the specific files and the statutory or Handbook text relied on.
Keep factual rebuttal separate from mitigation, since mixing them reads as arguing rather than correcting and hardens the department's position.
Where a criticism is accepted, state the remedial commitment and an indicative date in the response so the plan discussion starts from the company's own proposal.
Have the Head of Compliance approve, then file the response through the exam coordinator before the comment-window deadline and record the submission date and the department's acknowledgement.
checklist.done: a counsel-drafted, Head of Compliance approved response addressing every criticism was filed before the comment-window deadline with acknowledgement recorded.

checklist.step: Negotiate and execute the corrective action plan or consent order
actions: Agree with the department the corrective action for each surviving criticism, the completion date for each, the restitution basis and any monetary penalty.
Test each proposed date against the operating team's real capacity and system release calendar before agreeing it, since a missed agreed date is itself a violation.
Have Regulatory Counsel review every term for scope creep, in particular commitments that extend beyond the examined state or the examined period.
Execute the plan or order, record the execution date and distribute the executed document to every named owner the same day.
checklist.done: an executed corrective action plan or consent order exists with a dated commitment per criticism, capacity-tested and counsel-reviewed.

checklist.step: Build the remediation log with milestones, owners and evidence requirements
actions: Create one log row per commitment carrying the criticism reference, the agreed action text, the department-agreed date, the owner, the evidence artifact required to close it and the effectiveness test required.
Break any commitment longer than 60 days into interim milestones so slippage is visible before the agreed date rather than at it.
Configure reminders at 30, 14 and 3 days before each agreed date to the owner and the Compliance Manager.
Publish a weekly status showing every commitment as On track, At risk or Overdue, with At risk requiring a written recovery plan from the owner.
checklist.done: every commitment has a log row with an agreed date, owner, required evidence, interim milestones and configured reminders.

checklist.step: Fix the process and system root cause behind each agreed criticism
actions: For each agreed criticism write the root cause as a specific process step, system configuration or missing control, not as a training gap unless the evidence supports that.
Specify the change: a mandatory field, a workflow block, a template amendment to the denial or nonrenewal letter, a timeliness alert, or a supervisory approval step.
Raise the change through the normal release process with the exam reference attached so it is prioritised and traceable, and get the release date confirmed against the agreed milestone date.
Verify the change in the production environment with 10 live transactions after release and attach the verification evidence to the log row.
checklist.done: each agreed criticism has a named root cause, a released system or process change, and production verification on 10 live transactions.

checklist.step: Build the restitution population from the full examined period
actions: Define the affected population from the criticism itself: the state, line, transaction type and the period the department specified, and never narrow it to the examiner's sample.
Extract every consumer transaction meeting the definition with policy or claim number, insured name, address, transaction date, amount paid and amount that should have been paid.
Reconcile the population count and amount to the system of record control totals and have the Data Quality Analyst sign the reconciliation.
Have Regulatory Counsel confirm the population definition matches what the department ordered before any calculation begins.
checklist.done: the restitution population is extracted for the full ordered period, reconciled to system control totals and counsel-confirmed against the order.

checklist.step: Calculate the restitution amount including statutory interest
actions: Compute the shortfall per consumer as the amount that should have been paid less the amount paid, showing both figures on the record.
Apply the interest rate the state or the order specifies, running from the date the payment was due to the planned payment date, and show the day count and rate on each row.
Have a second preparer independently recompute a 10 percent sample of rows and reconcile any difference before the file is approved.
Produce the calculation summary by state and line with total consumers, total shortfall, total interest and total payable, and have the Controller confirm the accrual is booked.
checklist.done: a per-consumer calculation with shortfall, rate, day count and interest exists, independently recomputed on a 10 percent sample and accrued in the ledger.

checklist.step: Execute the restitution payments and consumer notices
actions: Issue payment to each consumer on the approved calculation file, using the address or payment instruction validated against the policy record, and record the payment reference and date per row.

Send the accompanying notice using the wording the department approved, explaining what was corrected, the period covered and the interest included, and never wording that requires a release or waiver in exchange.
Reconcile payments issued to the calculation file daily until every row is paid or exhausted, and track returned and uncashed payments as open rows.
Complete all payments before the order's restitution completion date and produce the payment register as the proof.
checklist.done: every consumer on the calculation file is paid with a recorded payment reference and an approved notice, completed before the ordered date.

checklist.step: Work the unlocatable consumers and escheat what cannot be paid
actions: For each returned or uncashed payment run an address search through the policy record, the claim file and a licensed locator service, and record each search attempt with its date and result.
Reissue payment on any successful trace and keep the row open until the payment clears.

Where the consumer cannot be located after the searches the order or the state requires, escheat the amount to the state unclaimed property administrator under its dormancy rules and record the escheat reference.
Report the located, reissued and escheated counts and amounts to the Compliance Manager for the proof-of-compliance package.
checklist.done: every unpaid row is either traced and reissued or escheated with a recorded reference, and no row is simply written back.

checklist.step: Pay any monetary penalty and record it correctly
actions: Pay the penalty stated in the order to the department by its due date through the payment method the order specifies, and capture the remittance advice and the department's receipt.
Book the penalty to the regulatory fines account, not to loss expense, so it is visible in statutory reporting and to internal audit.
Confirm the amount and the paid date with Regulatory Counsel before payment, since an early or partial payment can be read as accepting terms not yet agreed.
File the remittance and receipt in the exam folder against the penalty commitment row.
checklist.done: the penalty is paid by its due date to the specified account, booked to regulatory fines and evidenced by a receipt in the exam folder.

checklist.step: Update the procedures and retrain the affected teams
actions: Have the affected procedure rewritten to reflect the corrected practice and re-approved before the training is built, so training and procedure cannot diverge.
Build a module covering what the examiner found, why it was a violation and exactly what changes at the desk, using real anonymised examples from the criticised files.
Assign it to every performer in the affected function and state, with a completion due date at least 30 days before the commitment date, and require a passing assessment.
Export the completion report and attach it to the commitment row as closure evidence.
checklist.done: the revised procedure is approved, training is completed and passed by every affected performer, and the completion report is attached.

checklist.step: Run the post-implementation effectiveness test before closing any criticism
actions: For each criticism, wait at least 60 days after the fix is live and draw a fresh sample of 30 transactions processed after the change.
Test them against the same standard the examiner applied and compute the post-fix error rate.
Compare it to the examiner's error rate and require a demonstrated fall to the agreed tolerance, commonly under 3 percent, before the criticism may be closed.
Where the error rate has not fallen, reopen the root cause rather than closing on the fact that the change was released.
checklist.done: each criticism has a post-fix sample of 30 transactions with a computed error rate at or below the agreed tolerance before closure.

checklist.step: File the proof-of-compliance report with the department on the ordered date
actions: Assemble the package: the commitment-by-commitment status, the restitution completion certificate with consumer and amount totals, the payment register summary, the escheat summary, the training completion report and the effectiveness test results.
Have the Head of Compliance sign the certification and Regulatory Counsel clear every statement of completion, since an overstated closure is a fresh violation.
File it through the exam coordinator by the ordered date using the channel the order specifies, and record the filing date and the department's acknowledgement.
Track the department's review and answer any follow-up question inside the window it sets.
checklist.done: a signed, counsel-cleared proof-of-compliance package was filed by the ordered date with the department's acknowledgement recorded.

checklist.step: Close the exam, retain the evidence and arm the repeat-finding check
actions: Move the full exam record into the compliance evidence repository under Market Conduct / Exams / <state> <exam year>: reports, responses, the executed plan or order, restitution files, payment proofs, escheat references, training and effectiveness test results and the closure acknowledgement.
Apply the 7-year-from-exam-close retention label and keep the legal hold in place until counsel releases it.
Add every closed criticism to the prior-findings pack used for exam readiness so the next exam in any state starts with the repeat-finding check done.
Set an annual re-test task on each closed criticism for two years so a decayed fix is found by the company and not by the next examiner.
checklist.done: the exam record is archived under a 7-year label, added to the prior-findings pack and each closed criticism carries a two-year annual re-test task.

testing.step: Build the population of criticisms and corrective action commitments
actions: Read the final examination report and the executed corrective action plan or consent order directly and list every criticism and every commitment from the source documents.
Extract the remediation log and join it to your independently built list on criticism reference.
List any criticism or commitment absent from the log, and any log row with no counterpart in the order, as automatic exceptions.
Sign the population as complete, naming the report and order versions used.
testing.done: every criticism and commitment in the source documents is matched to a remediation log row, or the gap is listed.

testing.step: Recompute every milestone date against the department-agreed date
actions: For each commitment read the agreed date from the executed order rather than from the log, since a log date can drift.
Compare the closure date recorded on the log to the agreed date and compute days early or late for every commitment.
For any late closure, look for a written department extension with a date and an approver; treat an unevidenced extension as a missed date.
Recompute the comment-window and response dates from the draft report receipt date and confirm the response was filed inside the window.
testing.done: every commitment carries a computed early or late figure against the order date, with each late closure either evidenced by an extension or logged as a fail.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of commitments and restitution rows
actions: Take 100 percent of commitments involving consumer restitution, a monetary penalty or a repeat of a prior finding.
Take 15 further commitments at random using a seeded, reproducible selection covering every criticised function.
Draw 40 consumer rows at random from the restitution population, stratified so the largest 10 amounts are included in full.
Record the seed, population sizes, selection date and the resulting lists in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, covers all restitution and penalty commitments and includes the 10 largest restitution amounts.

testing.step: Re-perform the restitution population definition against the order
actions: Read the population definition in the executed order and build the extract yourself from the warehouse for the ordered state, line, transaction type and period.
Compare your row count and total amount to the company's restitution population and investigate every difference.
Check specifically for a period narrowed to the examiner's sample window, a state list narrowed to the examined state where the order said otherwise, and excluded transaction types.
Treat any consumer in your population absent from the company's file as an unremediated consumer, not a documentation difference.
testing.done: the independently built restitution population reconciles to the company's file, or every missing consumer is quantified and named as unremediated.

testing.step: Recompute the restitution amounts and interest on the sample
actions: For each of the 40 sampled consumers pull the underlying transaction and recompute the amount that should have been paid from the policy terms and the filed rate or the claim entitlement.
Recompute the shortfall, then recompute interest using the rate the order specifies, the due date and the actual payment date.
Compare to the company figure and treat any underpayment, any missing interest and any interest run to the planned rather than the actual payment date as an exception.
Capture the recomputation workbook with the source transaction extracts into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled restitution amount and interest figure recomputes to the paid amount, or the shortfall is quantified per consumer.

testing.step: Trace the sampled restitution rows to cleared payments and approved notices
actions: For each sampled consumer trace the payment reference to a cleared payment in the payment system with a date on or before the ordered completion date.
Read the notice sent and confirm it uses the department-approved wording and does not condition payment on any release or waiver.
For returned or uncashed rows confirm the trace attempts are individually logged and that escheat, where applied, carries a state reference and respects the dormancy period.
List any consumer with no cleared payment, no escheat and no open trace as an unremediated consumer.
testing.done: every sampled consumer is traced to a cleared payment, an escheat reference or an open documented trace, with approved notice wording confirmed.

testing.step: Re-perform the post-implementation effectiveness test on a fresh sample
actions: For 5 sampled commitments draw your own sample of 30 transactions processed at least 60 days after the fix went live.
Test each against the standard the examiner applied and compute your own error rate.

Compare it to the company's reported post-fix error rate and to the examiner's original rate, and treat a company rate materially better than yours as an effectiveness testing exception in its own right.
Confirm the system or process change is actually present in production by inspecting the configuration or the letter template rather than relying on the release note.
testing.done: 5 commitments have an independently computed post-fix error rate and confirmed production presence of the change.

testing.step: Test the closure package, penalty payment and department acknowledgement
actions: Confirm the proof-of-compliance package was filed by the ordered date, is signed by the Head of Compliance and carries a recorded department acknowledgement.
Compare the totals certified in the package to the payment register, the escheat summary and the training completion report and treat any overstatement as a serious finding.
Trace the penalty payment to a cleared disbursement on or before its due date and confirm it is booked to the regulatory fines account rather than loss expense.
Confirm the exam record is archived with the 7-year label and that every closed criticism sits in the prior-findings pack with an annual re-test task.
testing.done: the closure package is timely, signed, acknowledged and reconciles to the underlying registers, and the penalty is paid on time and correctly booked.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the criticism reference, the commitment affected, the consumer or amount involved and the regulatory consequence.
Assign a root cause from the fixed set: population narrowed, interest miscalculated, payment not executed, milestone slipped, closure certified without evidence, fix ineffective.
Set an owner and a remediation date, and where a consumer was left unpaid or short-paid open a supplemental restitution run and a counsel-cleared self-report to the department.
Escalate any exception touching a certified closure to the Head of Compliance the same day, since the department has already been told the matter is closed.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and, where a certification was overstated, a counsel-cleared self-report plan.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report the remediation outcome
actions: Compute the on-time closure rate against department-agreed dates, the restitution completeness rate and the count of criticisms closed without an effective post-fix result.
Write the conclusion (remediation complete, complete with exceptions, or not complete) with the workpaper references supporting each measure.
Have the independent reviewer, who owned no remediation action and calculated no restitution, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion to the Compliance Committee and the Board Governance Lead where a consent order is involved, and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under the exam.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, on-time closure rate and restitution completeness rate exists in the repository with a committee reporting date.
